reviews.comment: He's a great lecturer but you have an ICE (in class assignment) every class. This was kind of annoying at times (I wish he made it to where we did the ICE assignments after doing homeworks on the topic) and had done them less (maybe once a week instead). Exams were pretty reasonable though and homeworks were effective though.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: You get out what you put in. All the material is taught well and the tests are reflective of the material taught. Exactly what teaching should be. Only downside is no computers or phones in class and attendance is mandatory.

Prof. Noshadravan makes dynamics what it should be. He doesn't give the hardest examples he can think of on exams. He doesn't overload us with homework on exam weeks. He doesn't expect us to study and work for 10 hours daily to pass the class. The work load and difficulty is manageable, and it is a nice change of pace from other profs at A&M.

Adv. Mechanics was one of the easiest course I had taken. Dr. Noshadravan is a great professor and keeps the homework and the assessments balanced with the classwork. He is approachable outside the classroom, posts all the relevant material online, and marks leniently. Take his course without a second thought if you want to learn and score.
He made the super critical "Structural Reliability" course very easy! He is one of a kind, he knows a lot. If you really want to learn something. take his course
Very organized during the COVID semester. The In-Class Exercises and homework assignments are very good ways to get practice for the tests. The tests are 3-5 questions long.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Noshadravan is a great professor. CVEN 305 is not an easy class with any professor. But his exams are similar to the homework, you can bring a cheat sheet, he marks leniently, so they're overall very doable. His lectures are good, and he posts the notes online. He does go a little fast though. In any case, I would highly recommend him.

Dr. Noshadravan was a good prof to take for this class, straight forward in class. Homework due periodically and in class exercises every monday. If you have to miss class though beware, if its not university excused he will not let you. Even if you offer to do the work ahead of time or ask to take the test early. He is a huge rule stickler.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY
